steps.text: Type a request in the Messages box.
The agent edits the script. The bracket is 1 in wider, with two mounting holes in the base.
It replies with what it changed.
Click a face to select it, then ask about "this face".
The agent reads the selection and puts two holes through that face.

steps_phone.text: Open Chat and type a request.
The agent edits the script. The bracket gets wider.
The agent replies. Close the sheet to see the holes.
Tap a face to select it.
The agent puts holes through the selected face.

setup.text: Have Claude Code installed. Cadpole uses your own install and ships no agent of its own.
Open your script in the web app.
Register Cadpole's MCP server, in your project folder.
setup.command: claude mcp add cadpole -- cadpole mcp
setup.note: This adds it for you in this folder (the local scope); --scope project writes it to .mcp.json for everyone on the project. claude mcp list checks the connection and claude mcp remove cadpole takes it out.

alt.summary: Another MCP client, or by hand: .mcp.json

setup.text: Start Claude Code in that folder and ask it to wait for Cadpole. It runs cadpole listen in the background, which costs nothing until you send a message.
setup.prompt: Wait for messages from Cadpole in the background and act on them.

setup.text: Turn Listen on in the web app and type in the Messages box.

can: It writes the model's script and changes it, one exact edit at a time.
Every error names the line and the feature it came from.
It measures clearances and volumes, renders pictures and runs the model's tests.
Click a face in the 3D view and say "this face".
setup_agent: Set up Cadpole's assistant integration from github.com/mikelikespie/cadpole (docs/assistant-integration.md): register its MCP server with claude mcp add, start cadpole serve on my script, and tell me when to restart you so you can wait for my messages.
